action_criteria.expected_evidence: No epidural haematoma, collection, hardware failure or cord compression; nerve root enhancement may be seen but is non-specific near the operative bed
action_criteria.label: Contrast MRI of the spine to exclude a postoperative compressive or infective complication
action_criteria.rationale: Leg weakness with severe pain two weeks after multilevel lumbar surgery raises epidural haematoma, abscess and hardware complications, which need imaging before the weakness is attributed to GBS and before a lumbar puncture near the operative field [EAN_PNS_2023, Leonhard_2019].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Polyradiculoneuropathy pattern (demyelinating or axonal features, absent F-waves, sural sparing where present); may be normal in the first week
action_criteria.label: Nerve conduction studies and needle EMG
action_criteria.rationale: Nerve conduction studies show the demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy and its extent beyond the operated levels, which a postoperative root injury does not produce [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Albuminocytological dissociation: raised protein with cells <5/mm3 (5-50/mm3 compatible but prompts an alternative; >50/mm3 suggests another diagnosis); protein may be normal in the first week
action_criteria.label: Lumbar puncture for CSF cell count, protein and glucose
action_criteria.rationale: CSF supports the diagnosis and excludes the infective causes of polyradiculopathy that raise the cell count [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Baseline values before treatment; abnormal liver tests or low albumin mark a higher risk of a severe course; no metabolic or toxic alternative
action_criteria.label: Baseline blood tests: full blood count, renal function and electrolytes, liver tests, albumin, glucose and CK
action_criteria.rationale: Routine blood tests exclude metabolic mimics and give the baseline before IVIg; liver tests and albumin carry prognostic weight [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: FVC in L, % predicted and mL/kg, MIP and MEP, with the trend; ICU-level monitoring if FVC <20 mL/kg or <60% predicted, MIP weaker than -30 cmH2O, MEP <40 cmH2O, a fall of more than 30%, or bulbar weakness with weak cough
action_criteria.label: Bedside respiratory function (FVC, MIP, MEP), repeated serially while weakness progresses
action_criteria.rationale: She cannot stand, is progressing and is breathless lying flat; serial FVC, MIP and MEP decide ICU-level monitoring and intubation planning [Lawn_2001, EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Continuous telemetry with blood pressure monitoring: sinus rhythm 62-102 bpm with sinus tachycardia during pain and blood pressure 126/72 to 168/94 mmHg in the first 24 hours; autonomic instability (rate and blood pressure lability, bradyarrhythmia) requires continued monitoring while weakness progresses
action_criteria.label: Continuous inpatient cardiac telemetry with blood pressure monitoring while weakness progresses
action_criteria.rationale: Autonomic dysfunction is common in GBS and can cause bradyarrhythmias, pauses and blood-pressure lability; monitoring continues while weakness progresses [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Normal sinus rhythm, rate 92, with normal PR, QRS and QTc (446 ms) as the baseline
action_criteria.label: Obtain a 12-lead ECG to screen for autonomic dysrhythmias and baseline QTc
action_criteria.rationale: A baseline 12-lead ECG screens for autonomic rhythm and conduction changes and gives the QTc before treatment [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: ACE inhibitor caution before albumin-replacement plasma exchange (hold lisinopril); IVIg thrombotic and renal warnings in an older immobile postoperative patient; nothing relevant with alendronate or acetaminophen
action_criteria.label: Check the medication list for interactions with lisinopril before plasma exchange and with IVIg in an immobile postoperative patient
action_criteria.rationale: Lisinopril changes the safety of albumin-replacement plasma exchange, and recent surgery with immobility raises the thrombotic risk of IVIg.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General evidence on immunotherapy in GBS; not needed for the diagnosis or the treatment decision
action_criteria.label: Optional literature search on IVIg versus plasma exchange in GBS
action_criteria.rationale: Background evidence only; not a clinical step of the work-up.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not treat with corticosteroids: oral corticosteroids are strongly advised against and IV methylprednisolone is not recommended [EAN_PNS_2023].
Do not start IVIg without checking renal function.
required_recommendations: Admit to ICU-level monitoring now (MIP -26 cmH2O, weaker than -30, MEP 42 cmH2O, FVC falling from 1.8 to 1.6 L, weak cough) with FVC, MIP and MEP every 2-4 hours; plan elective intubation if FVC falls below 20 mL/kg (about 1.2 L at 62 kg) or MIP and MEP keep falling, or cough, secretions, bulbar function or fatigue worsen, and intubate regardless of the numbers for respiratory distress, hypoxaemia or hypercapnia [EAN_PNS_2023, Lawn_2001].

Start IVIg 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (2 g/kg total, about 25 g/day at 62 kg) now, because she cannot walk and is within 2 weeks of onset; plasma exchange (200-250 mL/kg over 5 sessions) is an equivalent alternative, with lisinopril held for 24 hours before albumin-replacement exchange [EAN_PNS_2023].
Continuous cardiac telemetry with blood pressure monitoring while weakness progresses.
Thromboprophylaxis: intermittent pneumatic compression now and subcutaneous low-molecular-weight heparin once the spinal surgeon confirms it is safe, while she cannot walk [Leonhard_2019].
Review with the spinal surgical team (wound, hardware, timing of anticoagulant prophylaxis and of any procedure).

avoided_actions.rationale: GBS is a peripheral nerve / nerve-root disorder; EEG has no role in diagnosis unless atypical CNS features (encephalopathy, seizures) are present.
Echocardiography is not indicated in typical GBS; reserve for pre-existing cardiac disease or unexplained hemodynamic instability after autonomic causes are excluded.
Head CT contributes no diagnostic information in GBS; the disease is peripheral and CT does not visualise nerve roots reliably.
Brain MRI is reserved for atypical features (encephalopathy, CNS signs, transverse myelitis on differential). In classic GBS it does not aid diagnosis.

accepted: Guillain-Barré syndrome (acute inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy) after spinal surgery

differential.diagnosis: Epidural haematoma or other postoperative spinal compression
differential.key_features: Pain and leg weakness after multilevel surgery raise it, but the hand weakness and arm hyporeflexia lie above the operated levels, there is no sensory level or sphincter dysfunction, and contrast MRI shows no haematoma, collection or cord compression.
Would be restricted to the operated roots and present from surgery; symmetric ascending weakness reaching the hands after an asymptomatic interval, with demyelinating NCS, excludes it.
Afebrile, wound healing well, CSF acellular, no collection or abnormal enhancement on MRI; CRP and ESR are modestly raised, as expected two weeks after surgery.
Perineal sensation, anal tone and bladder emptying are normal, and the arms are involved.
No ICU course before onset; uncomplicated surgery and ward recovery.
Cannot be excluded at presentation; progression beyond 8 weeks or 3 or more treatment-related fluctuations would point to it. Reassess at 8 weeks.

key_clinical_evidence: Surgery is a recognised antecedent event of GBS; weakness that begins after an asymptomatic postoperative interval and spreads beyond the operated segments is not a surgical root injury.
Contrast spine MRI excludes an epidural haematoma, collection or hardware complication; postoperative root enhancement near the operative bed is non-specific.

Ascending weakness reaching the hands with areflexia, CSF albuminocytological dissociation (protein 86 mg/dL, 3 cells/mm3) and a demyelinating NCS with sural sparing: Brighton level 1 once the course plateaus within 4 weeks [Brighton_2011].
A single loose stool is not a diarrhoeal illness. The antecedent infection is a history finding; serology is not needed for the diagnosis, and a positive IgM does not prove the trigger.
MIP -26 cmH2O and a falling FVC call for ICU-level monitoring even with FVC still above 20 mL/kg [Lawn_2001, EAN_PNS_2023].

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: The MRI excludes a compressive or infective complication; ascending weakness reaching the hands with areflexia, CSF dissociation and demyelinating NCS indicates GBS after surgery, not surgical injury.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchors on a mechanical or surgical complication rather than an autoimmune polyradiculoneuropathy.
red_herrings.location: Past medical history and history of present illness

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: A single loose stool without fever or further diarrhoea is non-specific and does not count as a diarrhoeal illness; antecedent-infection testing is not needed for the diagnosis or the treatment decision.
red_herrings.data_point: Single loose stool on postoperative day 9
red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggests a Campylobacter trigger to be confirmed with stool culture or serology.

sequence_constraints.reason: Image the operated lumbar spine before the lumbar puncture: an epidural haematoma or collection changes the diagnosis and the safety and route of the puncture.
Renal function and the blood count are reviewed with the medication list before IVIg or plasma exchange is chosen.

interactions: Lisinopril (ACE inhibitor) and albumin-replacement plasma exchange: ACE inhibition blocks bradykinin breakdown and is associated with flushing, hypotension and bradycardia during apheresis; the ACE inhibitor is usually held for at least 24 hours before an exchange (category-level caution).

IVIg: thromboembolic events are reported, with higher risk in older patients, immobility, recent surgery and hyperviscosity; ensure adequate hydration and use the lowest practical infusion rate (product labelling warning).
IVIg and renal function: renal dysfunction is reported, more often with sucrose-stabilised products; concurrent ACE inhibitor is a relative caution, monitor creatinine.
general.proposed: IVIg or albumin-replacement plasma exchange; current medicines lisinopril, alendronate, acetaminophen
general.summary: Two category-level cautions: an ACE inhibitor with albumin-replacement plasma exchange (bradykinin-mediated reactions), and the thrombotic and renal warnings of IVIg, which weigh more after recent surgery and with immobility.
warnings: No interaction identified between IVIg or plasma exchange and alendronate or acetaminophen.

ecg.interpretation: Normal sinus rhythm, rate 92. Normal PR, QRS and QTc (446 ms) intervals. No acute ST-T changes.

labs.interpretation: Mild anaemia (Hb 11.8 g/dL). CRP 9.2 mg/L and ESR 44 mm/hr (elevated). Remaining values within reference ranges.

results.finding: Guidelines for adults with GBS who cannot walk unaided advise IVIg 2 g/kg over 5 days within 2 weeks of onset or plasma exchange within 4 weeks, with no preference between them; corticosteroids are not advised.
A second IVIg course in patients with a poor predicted prognosis did not improve outcome and caused more serious adverse events.

general.summary: IVIg or plasma exchange is advised for adults with GBS unable to walk unaided; neither is preferred, and a second IVIg course is not advised [EAN_PNS_2023, Walgaard_2021].

specialized_test.impression: This is an ABNORMAL study. 1. Prolonged distal motor latencies, reduced conduction velocities and temporal dispersion in median and peroneal motor nerves. 2. Reduced median with normal sural sensory amplitudes. 3. Absent peroneal and prolonged median F-waves; absent H-reflexes. 4. Reduced recruitment without denervation on needle EMG. Findings are consistent with an acute demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy. Clinical correlation recommended.

metadata.difficulty_description: GBS two weeks after lumbar spinal surgery: a postoperative compressive or infective complication is excluded with contrast spine MRI before the polyradiculoneuropathy is confirmed with NCS and CSF; respiratory function already calls for ICU-level monitoring.
metadata.difficulty_rationale: 6 required actions (NCS/EMG, CSF, baseline labs, respiratory function, telemetry, interaction check for lisinopril and IVIg) plus recommended spine MRI; 2 red herrings (recent surgery, single loose stool).
metadata.revision_reason: Reviewer 2 GBS audit: spine MRI is optional and limited to five cases with a concrete cord, traumatic, postoperative or infiltrative alternative; generic hidden MRI reports removed.

patient.chief_complaint: Bilateral thigh pain and tingling in the feet starting on postoperative day 11 after L1-L5 laminectomy, followed by ascending leg weakness; since yesterday she cannot stand.

past_medical_history: Lumbar spinal stenosis L1-L5 with L4/5 spondylolisthesis: L1-L5 laminectomy with L4/5 posterolateral fusion 14 days ago

patient.history_present_illness: Mrs. T. is a 78-year-old woman seen on postoperative day 14 after an uncomplicated L1-L5 laminectomy with L4/5 posterolateral fusion for lumbar spinal stenosis and spondylolisthesis. She had been walking with a walker and progressing as expected. On postoperative day 9 she had a single loose stool without fever, abdominal pain or further diarrhoea. On postoperative day 11 she developed severe bilateral thigh pain and tingling in both feet, followed over the next three days by ascending weakness of both legs and, since this morning, clumsiness of both hands. Since yesterday she cannot stand or walk. She has no back pain at the operated level beyond the expected incisional discomfort, no urinary retention or incontinence and no bowel change since the single loose stool. She has no double vision, facial weakness or difficulty swallowing, and reports mild breathlessness when lying flat. She is afebrile and her wound is healing well.

neurological_exam.additional: Surgical wound healing well, no erythema, tenderness or fluctuance. Perineal sensation intact; normal anal tone; bladder scan post-void residual 40 mL.
neurological_exam.coordination: Cannot assess lower limbs. Upper limbs intact.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Intact. No facial weakness, ophthalmoparesis or bulbar weakness.
neurological_exam.motor: Bilateral lower extremity weakness: hip flexion 3/5, knee extension 3/5, ankle dorsiflexion 3/5. Upper extremity distal: 4/5 bilaterally.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Absent bilateral patellar and Achilles. Trace bilateral upper extremity reflexes.
neurological_exam.sensory: Hyperaesthesia and allodynia of the distal legs and feet with bilateral tingling. Vibration reduced at the toes. No sensory level.
